alternatives.transcript: I've been thinking a lot lately about how technology has changed the way we form a critic opinions. When I was younger, I used to believe that social media will bring people closer together, and in some way, it has. But what I didn't expect was that I it would be so also create these very isolated bubbles where people only hear what they already agree with. I actually changed my mind completely about this after reading about recommendation algorithms work. The more you engage with certain content, the more of it you see, which means your work view narrows without you even realizing it. What I find particularly troubling is that this doesn't just affect us. We think it affects how we think. We lose the habit of sitting with uncertainty of considering that we might be wrong. I think if I could go back, I would have been much more deliberate about seeking out perspectives that challenged me.

summary.short: The speaker discusses how technology has changed the way people form critic opinions, creating isolated bubbles where people only hear what they agree with. The speaker believes that engaging in certain content, even if it wasn't previously considered a recommendation, has the potential to lead to narrowing one's workview without realizing it. The speaker believes that this change is not just affecting people, but also leaving them hungry for the views they consider.
